title: Diversity of Materials
seo_title: Primary 3 Science: Diversity of Materials Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_text: Identify common materials (wood, metal, plastic, glass, ceramic, rubber, fabric) and relate their uses to their properties: strength, flexibility, waterproof, transparency, hardness and the ability to float or sink. Carry out fair tests to compare materials (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on materials and their properties: strength, flexibility, waterproof, transparency, floating and sinking, with fair-test tables. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: We choose materials for their properties.
key_sub: Strength, flexibility, waterproof, transparency and floating.
body_html:
How to think about it

Objects are made of materials. We choose a material because of its properties.

  • Common materials: wood, metal, plastic, glass, ceramic, rubber and fabric.
  • Properties: strength, flexibility, waterproof, transparency, hardness and the ability to float or sink.
  • To compare materials fairly, change only the material and keep everything else the same.
Example

Why is a raincoat made of plastic?

It must keep rain out

Plastic is waterproof and flexible

Answer: Because plastic is waterproof and flexible.

Example

A strip of nylon held 20 kg and a strip of paper held 2 kg. Which is stronger?

Compare the masses held

20 kg is more than 2 kg

Answer: Nylon.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking heavy things always sink. A big log floats; a small key sinks.
  • Mixing up strong and hard. Glass is hard but breaks easily.
  • Changing two things at once in a test (for example the material and the size of the strip).
  • Choosing a material because it looks nice instead of because of its properties.

faq.q: What are the properties of materials in Primary 3?
faq.a: Strength, flexibility, hardness, waterproof, transparency and the ability to float or sink.
No. Whether an object floats depends on its material and shape. A large wooden log floats, but a small metal key sinks.

faq.q: How do I make a materials test fair?
faq.a: Change only the material. Keep the size of each piece, the amount of water or mass, and the way you test it the same.
